Pilot 1.3.1

18 November 2026

A bell in the dock, two clipboard actions, and fixes.

  • Updating from 1.2.0 or 1.3.0 keeps Pilot's permissions. From 1.1.1, macOS sees Pilot as a new app once (it is signed and notarized since 1.2.0), so allow Accessibility and the rest again when Pilot asks.
  • Notifications in the dock: pick Dock in Menu bar › Notifications › Show in, and a bell with the count sits at the end of Pilot's dock, each card rising over it.
  • Clipboard: Cmd+K on an image marks it up in the capture editor, and on a text saves it as a snippet.
  • Fixed: the floating bell's count is no longer cut off, apps and vaults can join your themes while one is applied, a theme change reloads every open Ghostty, and Pilot's dock keeps track of Pilot and of the apps you took out.
Download Pilot 1.3.1Its page on GitHub→

Pilot 1.3.0

17 November 2026

Liquid Glass, a widget grid, and your packs in the catalogue.

  • Updating from 1.2.0 keeps Pilot's permissions. From 1.1.1, macOS sees Pilot as a new app once (it is signed and notarized since 1.2.0), so allow Accessibility and the rest again when Pilot asks.
  • Liquid Glass: the dock, the top bar's islands and pills, widget tiles and dropdowns wear clear glass like the macOS Dock's. One Material in Look sets Glass, Solid or Clear for every surface. A violet icon, and light themes such as Meadow turn the bar's text white over a dark wallpaper.
  • Desktop: widgets snap to a grid as you Hyper+drag them, the Widgets page is a map of your display, the dock hides on a full-screen Space, and a click on a minimised app brings its window back.
  • Top bar: one Full strip preset, Attached or Floating; pills tone the wallpaper like the islands; clicks in the edge margin and on clear parts reach the bar, and a grouped item's dropdown opens under it.
  • Windows: drag apps between workspaces on the Workspaces page to move or swap them, windows and all. Windows and Look are areas of their own in Pilot's window.
  • Themes: favourites, a Themes tab that opens fast, and deleting a pack asks first. Send a theme or extension to the catalogue as a pull request (CONTRIBUTING says how): Pilot opens it for you from an account that can push. Pilot's code and its catalogue are one public repo, banozz0/pilot.
  • Ask Pilot: an Answer style (Blocks, Plain short or Detailed), a change you name is made straight away with the Allow card as your yes, and making a widget or extension works again.
  • Also: the capture editor's Mark up and Frame modes, the menu's layout in Launcher › More, CoreServices apps such as Keychain Access in the launcher, and images paste into a terminal as their file paths.
Its page on GitHub→

Pilot 1.2.0

14 November 2026

A dock of your own, new layouts, notarized.

  • Signed and notarized by Apple: Pilot opens like any app you download, with one question from macOS the first time. macOS sees it as a new app once, so allow Accessibility and the other permissions again when Pilot asks.
  • A dock of your own, switched on in Desktop › Dock: your Dock's apps then the running ones, icons tinted in your theme, magnification, a visualizer, widgets on either side, Attached to the screen's edge or Floating. Drag apps and widgets to rearrange them, and the top bar's items too.
  • New layouts: Main + stack split the way you would, Centred main for wide monitors, and Scrolling with three pictures to pick from. Click the workspace number in the top bar to cycle its layout.
  • Top bar groups: put any items in one pill, workspaces, Pilot's icon and the app's menus included. Floating strip and Three islands bars, Three islands Attached too.
  • Themes: 29 to get from Look › Themes, twelve new with wallpapers made for Pilot. Apply theme colours Ghostty, Zed, Obsidian, VS Code, Cursor, Kitty, btop, fish, lazygit, Neovim, Vesktop and more, each found by itself; a light theme can switch macOS to Light mode. Make and share your own packs.
  • Notifications as glass cards, floating or in the top bar, off until you switch them on in Menu bar › Notifications.
  • Also: Pilot Files in floating windows, Pilot's own image viewer, Upscale › Monitor for your screen's size, an AI fallback in AI › Setup, and removing an app offers its leftover files.
Its page on GitHub→

Pilot 1.1.1

6 November 2026

A smaller, quicker Pilot.

  • Pilot is 16 MB smaller (61 MB, was 77): the terminal downloads on its first Hyper+T (5 MB), checked against Pilot's own signature, and leaner art and updater files.
  • Quicker: the keyboard is ready first at launch, voices and dictation skip work they already did, and the calendar widget no longer holds up the app.
  • The clock's calendar: a reminder due at midnight shows on its day, and "party tonight 1:30" means 01:30, after midnight.
Its page on GitHub→

Pilot 1.1

5 November 2026

Cursors, Pilot Files and two new editors.

  • Cursor sets: Quiet, Toybox, Duo and Classic everywhere in macOS, in their own colours, your theme's or two you pick, with a trail and halos.
  • Pilot Files: a file window of its own with folder sizes, ⌘K on every file, new files from templates, cut and paste, and ⌘Z for every action.
  • The capture editor: uncrop by dragging an edge out, marks on the backdrop, edges that snap, a magnifier, bent arrows and a smooth pen.
  • The record editor: split, cut and speed up parts, the pointer drawn by Pilot (smooth, bigger, a click ring), vertical and square.
  • Words after an alias: tr hello translates, bw generate password lists that app's actions, em funny finds emoji, gif cat searches GIPHY.
  • Every app's actions in Hyper+Space, closed apps too once they have run.
  • A shorter setup: Set up everything in one click, each step shown and undoable, and Allow the rest walks each permission.
  • Folder designs by kind: 54 designs, and each known folder suggests its own.
  • Also: Tailscale in the top bar, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth switches, a CI widget, Pilot opens .txt and .md files, copied secrets expire, clipboard search in plain words, reminders from a quick note.
Its page on GitHub→

Install Pilot 1.3.1.

Free and open source. Needs macOS 27 or later on Apple silicon.

  1. 1DownloadDrag Pilot to Applications
  2. 2Open PilotClick Open when macOS asks, once
  3. 3Pick your Hyper keyAnd allow Accessibility
Details
  1. Download Pilot.dmg, open it and drag Pilot to Applications.
  2. Open Pilot. macOS asks once whether to open an app downloaded from the Internet: click Open.
  3. Pick your Hyper key in Pilot's setup and allow Accessibility. Hyper+Space opens the menu.

Signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Updates install from inside Pilot.

Permissions and checking the download

  • Accessibility: Pilot needs it to see your keys and move windows; nothing works without it.
  • Full Disk Access for file search in the menu, and System Events for sleep, restart and dark mode.
  • Microphone for dictation and an AI provider for the AI chat, both optional.
  • Input Monitoring only if Pilot asks, when you bind a mouse's media buttons.
  • Screen Recording when you first take a screenshot or recording, or turn on Menu bar › Other apps › Show exact menu bar items. macOS applies it after Pilot reopens: click Quit & Reopen.

Caps Lock as Hyper: tapped alone it is Escape, and Shift+Caps Lock still types capitals. Password fields are blind to every key tap on macOS, Pilot's included: your binds do not work while one has focus.

Updates keep the permissions you gave. Check the download against the .sha256 beside it on the Releases page: shasum -a 256 -c Pilot.dmg.sha256.
